newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn warns German tourists in Kenya to stay inside.
newsitem.headline: Bonn warns German tourists in Kenya to stay inside.

text.p: The German foreign ministry on Monday warned several thousand German tourists currently on holiday in Kenya to stay in their hotels and take precautions as a result of the violence in parts of the country.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that Bonn was not advising Germans to leave Kenya, which is visited by about 100,000 German citizens each year. There were several thousand in the country at the moment, he said.

"The situation has deteriorated considerably," the spokesman said. "The violence hasn't been directed towards tourists and no tourists have yet been hurt. We are advising tourists to Kenya not to leave their hotels and follow the instructions of their guides."
At least 33 people have been killed in the last five days in Kenya amid an outbreak of violence and thuggery.
President Daniel arap Moi has blamed the violence on opposition leaders fanning tribal hatred ahead of elections.

Some opposition leaders accuse Moi's ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) of orchestrating the well-planned attacks which began with the killing of six police and eight civilians on Wednesday in raids on two police posts south of Mombasa.
